items.title: 61529_Maxine Sullivan oral history interview
items.q: The interviewer states 'He accompanied Joe Turner', and the interviewee responds with a general philosophical statement about musicians being 'simpatico' without confirming personal involvement or specific knowledge of Joe Turner.

ctx.x: Oh, well, there are a few recordings that Art made with the rhythm section and they couldn't keep up with Art because he was so spontaneous. I mean there was no way that you could keep up with what was going on in his head. And of course that stuff was never written down. The guys get in there, they just have to follow or else and if you listen closely there were a lot of times when they couldn't keep up with Art and his changes, you know, they just had to lay out.

Well, that's been said about him but I think some people would say that he was also a good small group player when he accompanied -- well later on in his career he played with Ben Webster, with Roy Eldridge He accompanied Joe Turner, the blues singer --

I believe that -- you know there's a certain area where musicians and performers are simpatico, they can almost anticipate what the other person is going to play -- if you understand their basic, their progressions, they know how far they can improvise and how far they can
